title: Farzi
hook: How does Farzi Season 1 end? Sunny is cornered when a white Fortuner is traced on a phone call, fake currency flies out of a moving car as police close in, and Mansoor finally faces Sunny one-on-one - the swagger is gone and the damage is in the room.

sections.heading: The white Fortuner and the trap closing
sections.body: The finale opens on silence, not action. A white Fortuner is named on a phone call and the episode snaps shut around Sunny. The choice that sealed his fate was removing the tracker from Megha's phone - a decision that looked like protection and reads, in retrospect, as the key that unlocked the end. Police close in. Firoz panics. The calm confidence of the earlier episodes is gone because the infrastructure of escape has been quietly dismantled by the STF while the show was watching Sunny believe he was still two moves ahead.

sections.heading: Fake notes and the collapse of the counterfeit empire
sections.body: Fake currency spills out of a moving car as Sunny tries to run. The image is both literal and thematic: the thing he built, the art he turned into a criminal operation, becomes visible and disposable in the same moment. Every escape attempt narrows the road. Raj and DK direct the finale with the same tonal fluency that made the series work - the comedy of confidence curdling into the procedural logic of consequence. The counterfeit empire does not fall dramatically. It empties out.

sections.heading: Mansoor and Sunny face each other
sections.body: Mansoor, played by Vijay Sethupathi's obsessive STF officer, finally meets Sunny in the room the series has been building toward. The swagger Sunny carried through seven episodes is gone. The damage is sitting between them. The episode refuses to play the confrontation as a villain-vs-hero showcase. Mansoor is not triumphant. Sunny is not broken in any redemptive way. Two people who each believed their logic was irrefutable are looking at the cost of that belief. The finale leaves Sunny facing the system he tried to beat.

sections.heading: Season 1 closes, Season 2 confirmed
sections.body: Farzi Season 1 ends with Sunny in custody and the STF's case substantially closed. The series was confirmed as the most-watched Hindi web series of 2023, with a reported 37.1 million viewers. Season 2 was confirmed in production, with Raj and DK posting a teaser image on the show's third anniversary in February 2026, and Shahid Kapoor confirming principal photography. The ending is designed to resolve the immediate arc while leaving space for what follows.

final_image: Sunny and Mansoor face each other in a room stripped of bravado, with the fake currency, the burned bridges, and the cost of every decision between them.

lingering_questions.q: Does Sunny get arrested at the end of Farzi Season 1?
lingering_questions.a: Yes. Sunny is cornered in the finale after police trace a vehicle connected to him. He faces STF officer Mansoor in a direct confrontation and ends the season in custody.

lingering_questions.q: What was Sunny's critical mistake in Farzi Season 1?
lingering_questions.a: Removing the tracking device from Megha's phone, a decision the finale uses as the key that allowed police to close in. It looked like protection at the time and cost him his escape route.
Yes. Season 2 was confirmed in production by creators Raj and DK. As of June 2026, Shahid Kapoor has confirmed filming has begun. No premiere date has been announced.

lingering_questions.q: Who plays the antagonist in Farzi Season 1?
lingering_questions.a: Vijay Sethupathi plays Mansoor, the STF officer obsessively pursuing Sunny. Shahid Kapoor plays Sunny, the street artist turned counterfeiter.
